title: A vendor bill on an internal work order posts to the category's account
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the Internal Work Orders setting is on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Make sure the test location is connected to QuickBooks Online, with Inventory Asset and Cost of Parts mapped on its ShopView Accounts page, and that AccountingHub is not enabled.
  • Have access to the QuickBooks Online company of the test location, so its journal entries can be read.
  • Make sure the General Internal category is mapped to an expense account, account X, at the test location.
  • Have a new customer for this test, customer A, flagged as an Internal customer.
  • Have a new internal work order for this test, work order 1, for internal customer A, in status Approved, with one special-order part received against it, no bill yet.
custom_steps:
1. Enter the vendor bill for work order 1's special-order part at $125.00.
  2. In QuickBooks Online, open that vendor bill.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The bill is saved.

Step 2:

  • The bill line is posted to account X instead of Cost of Parts.
  • The bill keeps its vendor and its $125.00 total and credits Accounts Payable.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11764 (Story 7, QuickBooks Online sync)

  • S7-R3: “When a vendor bill is created for a special-order part or a sublet on a work order that is already internal or no charge, the bill line posts to the mapped expense account instead of Cost of Parts (or the category account); the vendor, the bill and Accounts Payable are unchanged. This covers the bill of a vendor-bought job entered as a special-order part (sublet, Terminology) and the vendor's core charge (S2-E7).”
  • Terminology: “Inventory part / special-order part / sublet → a part picked from stock; a part ordered from a vendor for this work order and received against it; work done by an outside vendor and billed to the shop. Special orders and sublets have vendor bills. Sublet is work bought from another vendor and entered as a special-order part; the product has no separate sublet line or part type, so every sublet rule in this PRD is the special-order rule.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
